info.name: ERPAPI (MassERP)
info.description: MassERP API. 1) Set collection variables loginId/password to a TEST ADMIN account (holds every permission after script 014). 2) Run 'Authentication > Login - Valid' (saves accessToken). 3) Run the folders. For the restricted-employee check set limitedPassword and run 'Access check (Test Employee27)' in order. Never commit real credentials.

Employees
item.description: Requires Bearer token (run Login - Valid first). Permissions: hr.employees.view (list / lookups / detail), .create, .edit, .deactivate (activate / deactivate); sending a 'login' section also needs company.users.manage.

exec: pm.test('Has branches/departments/nationalities/statuses', () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.branches).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(d.departments).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(d.nationalities).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(d.statuses).to.be.an('array'); });

item.name: Branches (Company)
item.description: Dhaval Branches.aspx ('Company' screen). Permissions: company.branches.view (read), company.branches.manage (write).

query.description: name / code / contact person / mobile / email

item.name: Shifts
item.description: Shift templates (tbl_Shift, script 004). Permissions: hr.attendance.shifts.view (read), hr.attendance.shifts.manage (write). Times HH:mm (24-hour); early punch-in / late grace default 15 minutes. End before start = night shift ending the next day (script 005); equal start and end is rejected.

item.name: Create - same start and end rejected (no write)

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 (not assigned) or 409 SHIFT_IN_USE', () => pm.expect([200, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: Employee Shifts
item.description: Shifts assigned to an employee for a date range (tbl_EmployeeShift, script 004). Permissions: hr.attendance.shifts.view (read), hr.attendance.shifts.manage (write). Max 3 shifts a day; punch windows (start - early punch-in .. end) must not overlap. Set shiftEmployeeId (the employee to assign) and run 'Shifts' first.

item.name: Attendance
item.description: Shift-wise punch in / out for the logged-in employee (login linked to an ACTIVE employee with a shift assigned today; permissions hr.attendance.self.view (today) and hr.attendance.self.punch (punch)). ONE endpoint for every button: POST /api/attendance/punch { action: punchIn | break | resume | punchOut, latitude, longitude }. Log in as the EMPLOYEE (not the admin) before running. Enable only the buttons in allowedActions.

exec: pm.test('A shift is completed with punchIn and punchOut', () => { pm.expect(shift).to.not.eql(undefined); pm.expect(shift.punchIn).to.not.eql(null); });

item.name: Punch in outside window / no shift - 409 (no write)
Permissions
item.description: Permission master (tbl_ApiPermission, scripts 009-014): permissionKey, permissionName, description. Read: company.access.users.view; write: company.access.permissions.manage (log in as an admin). Key: any text up to 100 characters, unique regardless of case, can be corrected later - except the 15 keys the API checks (seeded by script 014). No delete: deactivate / activate. These requests work on their own test key 'postman.test.permission' so real permissions are never switched off. Run 'List permissions' first: it sets permissionId (test key) and viewPermissionId / selfViewPermissionId / selfPunchPermissionId.

exec: if (id('postman.test.permission')) pm.collectionVariables.set('permissionId', id('postman.test.permission')); // lets the requests below run again

item.name: Create - duplicate key, other case (no write)
Create - key longer than 100 characters (no write)
Update - key used by another permission (no write)
Update - rename a key the API checks (no write)
User Permissions
item.description: Permissions assigned to LOGINS (tbl_ApiUserPermission, script 013). Read: company.access.users.view; write: company.access.permissions.manage (log in as an admin). Target login = limitedUserId (43 = Test Employee27; for any employee use the employee detail's login.userId). Uses the test permission (run Permissions > List permissions / Create test permission first). Replacing a login's whole list is shown in 'Access check (Test Employee27)'.

item.name: Assign permission to the login (WRITES DATA)

exec: pm.test('Returns the login list incl. the permission', () => pm.expect(row).to.be.an('object'));

item.name: Assign again - already assigned is kept (no write)
List permissions of the employee's login
Me
item.description: The logged-in user's permission keys - Flutter shows only the screens these allow. Token only (no permission needed).

exec: pm.test('Same user as the token', () => pm.expect(d.userId).to.be.above(0));

item.name: Access check (Test Employee27)
item.description: Run in order. 1) As the ADMIN (accessToken): give Test Employee27 (limitedUserId 43) ONLY hr.employees.view. 2) Log in as the employee (limitedLoginId / limitedPassword - set the password first) - saved in limitedAccessToken, so the admin token is kept. 3) Read is allowed (200); create / edit / deactivate / other screens are refused (403 ACCESS_DENIED). 4) As the admin: give the attendance keys back. Run 'Permissions > List permissions' first (sets viewPermissionId etc.).
